extracted.intended_audience: Node.js/TypeScript backend developers integrating Prisma as an ORM
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for setting up and using Prisma (schema, client generation, and basic queries) in Node.js/TypeScript applications, plus community/contribution procedures. Covers data modeling, generating Prisma Client, example queries, and contribution/security reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisma toolkit components
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisma consists of Prisma Client, Prisma Migrate, and Prisma Studio as its major tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prisma Client is an auto-generated and type-safe query builder for Node.js & TypeScript; Prisma Migrate is a declarative data modeling & migration system; Prisma Studio is a GUI to view and edit data in your database. Use the appropriate tool for querying, migrations, and GUI-based data inspection respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisma schema must configure three things
rubrics_metrics.description: A Prisma schema file should configure a Data source, a Generator, and a Data model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data source: specifies your database connection (via an environment variable). Generator: indicates that you want to generate Prisma Client. Data model: defines your application models. The page emphasizes these three as the basic configuration points of every Prisma project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data model responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A model in the Prisma data model should represent a table in the underlying database and provide the foundation for queries in the Prisma Client API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design models to map to database tables and to reflect the queries your application will perform; relations, fields, and types in the model determine generated client APIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to obtain a data model
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two major workflows to get a data model into your Prisma schema: introspect an existing database or write the data model manually and map it using Prisma Migrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'prisma db pull' / introspection to generate models from an existing DB, or author models and use Prisma Migrate to apply changes to the database. Choose the workflow based on whether the database already exists or you control schema evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate Prisma Client after schema changes
rubrics_metrics.description: After you change your data model, you must manually re-generate Prisma Client to update the generated code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation of @prisma/client invokes 'prisma generate' automatically, but subsequent schema changes require running 'prisma generate' manually. Generated code is placed in node_modules/.prisma/client and exported by node_modules/@prisma/client/index.d.ts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install and instantiate Prisma Client
rubrics_metrics.description: Install @prisma/client and import/instantiate PrismaClient in your code to start sending queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation: npm install @prisma/client (invokes prisma generate). Import examples: `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'; const prisma = new PrismaClient()` or CommonJS `const { PrismaClient } = require('@prisma/client'); const prisma = new PrismaClient()`.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisma Client query behavior and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the generated Prisma Client API for CRUD operations; queries return plain JavaScript objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: findMany to retrieve all users; include relations with include: { posts: true }; filter with where and OR on title/content contains; create related records in a nested create; update by where and data. Note: all Prisma Client queries return plain old JavaScript objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage generated TypeScript types for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: When using TypeScript, Prisma's generated types make query results statically typed so you can't accidentally access non-existent properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the generated types (see Advanced usage of generated types) to catch typos at compile-time and get full type-safety even when retrieving subsets of model fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community support channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions and initiate discussions in the prisma repository on GitHub or join community Slack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README points to Slack and GitHub as places to ask questions and discuss Prisma-related topics. Use the repository 'prisma' to start issues or discussions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to create useful bug reports
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a bug report, include additional debugging output and other best-practice details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README links to docs with best practices for bug reports (e.g., include reproducible steps and debug logs). Following those practices increases the chance of swift triage and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting feature requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the roadmap to see if a feature is planned and, for linked GitHub issues, leave a +1 and a comment with your thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before filing a new feature request, search the roadmap and existing issues; add a +1 and constructive comment to indicate interest and provide context. This helps prioritize and consolidate demand for features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow contribution guidelines and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors should follow the project's contribution guidelines and the Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the repository's CONTRIBUTING and Code of Conduct documents for processes, required steps for PRs/issues, and expected community behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting security issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a security issue to report, contact security@prisma.io.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security vulnerabilities should be reported directly via the specified email address rather than public issue trackers to allow responsible disclosure and handling.
